key_insight: A Distil GPT2 table-to-text framework showed strong disease prediction performance on small clinical datasets, including thyroid cancer recurrence; it did not study drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: The approach may support research into prediction from limited, imbalanced clinical data, but clinical utility remains unproven.
method: Convert structured patient records into physician-style text.
Use GPT4-generated medical paraphrases to increase minority-class representation and fine-tune Distil GPT2.
Apply gradient-based explainability to identify influential clinical features.
evidence_signal: Across four public datasets covering heart disease, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, and thyroid cancer recurrence, reported average precision, specificity, sensitivity, and F1-score were 0.96, 0.97, 0.96, and 0.96, respectively.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify external validation or safeguards against leakage from paraphrased records, limiting confidence in real-world generalization.
paper_title: Can GPT Be Used as an Alternative Prediction Model to Traditional Machine Learning and Neural Networks on Low-Volume Clinical Data?
